title: Experimental evidence of an upper limit for hydrogen storage at 77 K on activated carbons
material_description: M1149 | activated carbon from Moszczenica (Polish) anthracite, prepared at Wroclaw University of Technology; KOH or NaOH chemical activation (hydroxide not specified per sample); label = precursor initial + S_BET in m2/g
purification_method: exposed to air humidity 1 day, washed with 1 M HCl then distilled water to constant pH ~6, oven-dried 24 h, sieved to 100-200 um
activation_method: chemical activation of the anthracite powder (100-200 um) physically mixed with NaOH or KOH lentils at XOH/anthracite mass ratios 1-3, heated under N2 to Ta = 973-1073 K and held 1 h (per-sample hydroxide, ratio and Ta not stated)
source_location: Table 2, p. 1908, row M1149, column 'At 298 K and 5 MPa (%) IJL volumetric device'
notes: Value printed as "0.4 +/- 0.1"; pressure printed as 5 MPa. wt% convention W1 stated: Table 2 caption "expressed as weight% of the outgassed activated carbons" (H2 mass as a percentage of outgassed carbon mass). IJL laboratory-made volumetric device (Section 2.3.1: stainless-steel vessel ~3 cm3, H2 introduced point by point, Hemmes EOS): outgassed 48 h under secondary vacuum (temperature not stated); H2 purity >5 N (99.999 stored as the lower bound); measurements corrected for gas compressed outside the vessel and cross-checked by water-column release (<3%), but how the free volume was determined is not described (calibration_described=false). Lab named after the corresponding author (V. Fierro, IJL). (1) with E0 from DR on N2; V_DR,CO2 (DR, CO2 at 273 K, range 4.2-9.9) stored in micropore_volume_co2_cm3_g: the paper says it reflects pores narrower than 0.7 nm, but it is not stored as an ultramicropore volume (it exceeds V_DR,N2 for M1149); samples outgassed 48 h at 523 K before N2/CO2.
basis_evidence: Table 2 caption: "Hydrogen uptake (excess) measured in different conditions, and expressed as weight% of the outgassed activated carbons." (excess named, not defined)
measuring_lab_id: Fierro group, Institut Jean Lamour (IJL), Nancy
